newsitem.title: USA: Gadzooks okay with $0.25/shr Q2 estimate.
newsitem.headline: Gadzooks okay with $0.25/shr Q2 estimate.

text.p: Gadzooks Inc said Tuesday that it is comfortable with analysts' earnings estimates of $0.25 per share for its second quarter.

"We're comfortable with $0.25 a share. Most analysts are in tune with what's going on," said Monty Standifer, Chief Financial Officer of Gadzooks at the PaineWebber Aggressive Growth & Technology Conference in New York.
He said he saw second quarter comparable store sales "in line" with first quarter's 4.4 percent increase.
Standifer said that he expects the company's operating margins to be flat in fiscal 1997 with 1996's margin 9.2 percent, due to cost of opening a new distribution center.
"Next year we will get back the 20 to 30 basis points that the distribution center cost us and we'll be well on the way towards the 10 percent operating margin that we've spoken about," he said.
For fiscal 1996, which ended February 1 1997, Gadzooks gross profit margin was 31.9 percent and selling, general and administrative costs was 22.7 percent of sales.
Chief Executive Jerry Szczepanski told investors that the company expects to open at least 64 stores in 1997, compared to 57 in 1996.
Current plans call for 27 new stores open for the back-to-school season and 23 open for the holidays, on top of the 14 new stores open for the spring.
Szczepanski said the company will probably open closer to 26 stores for the holiday season, with the 23 planned stores in current markets and the rest in a new market.
